questions.q: What is the primary difference between an economic activity and a non-economic activity?
questions.a: Economic activities are done for money or monetary value, while non-economic activities are done for personal care, love, or social service. A wrong answer here suggests the student is confusing "work" (effort) with "earning" (reward).

questions.q: If your neighbor spends their weekend painting your house for free because they are your friend, is this an economic activity? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is a non-economic activity because it is performed out of friendship/care and no money or payment was exchanged. A wrong answer shows the student thinks any "productive work" is an economic activity regardless of payment.

questions.q: A tailor stitches a school uniform and charges ₹200 for it. Identify the type of activity and explain the "value" involved.
questions.a: This is an economic activity. The value involves the exchange of service (stitching) for money (₹200). A wrong answer indicates difficulty linking "service" to "monetary compensation."

questions.q: Compare a doctor treating a patient in a private clinic versus a doctor volunteering at a free health camp. How do these compare in terms of economic classification?
questions.a: The first is an economic activity (earning a fee), while the second is non-economic (service to society). A wrong answer reveals an inability to see that the same profession can perform different types of activities based on payment status.

questions.q: "Economic activities are more important than non-economic activities because they generate wealth." Do you agree? Justify your answer.
questions.a: I disagree; while economic activities provide money for survival, non-economic activities (like parenting or volunteering) provide social and emotional support that is essential for a healthy society. A wrong answer shows a lack of appreciation for the "value of work" beyond money.

questions.q: Create a scenario where an activity changes from non-economic to economic.
questions.a: A student teaching their sibling math for free (non-economic) decides to start a tuition center and charges a monthly fee (economic). A poor answer fails to show the shift from "care" to "formal exchange of money."
